(3) We have that {𝐡π:π​ is connected set partition}\{\mathbf{h}_{\pi}:\pi\text{ is connected set partition}\} generates NCSym\mathrm{NCSym}. Also, 𝐡π⋅𝐡τ=𝐡π|τ\mathbf{h}_{\pi}\cdot\mathbf{h}_{\tau}=\mathbf{h}_{\pi|\tau}. Note that π|τ\pi|\tau is an odd set partition if and only if π\pi and τ\tau are odd set partitions. Consequently, the set {𝐡π:π​ is odd set partition}\{\mathbf{h}_{\pi}:\pi\text{ is odd set partition}\} can be generated by {𝐡π:π​ is connected odd set partition}\{\mathbf{h}_{\pi}:\pi\text{ is connected odd set partition}\}. Since ΘNCQSym\Theta_{\mathrm{NCQSym}} is an algebra epimorphism, the set {𝐪π:π​ is connected odd set partition}\{\mathbf{q}_{\pi}:\pi\text{ is connected odd set partition}\} generates {𝐪π:π​ is odd set partition}\{\mathbf{q}_{\pi}:\pi\text{ is odd set partition}\} and NC​Ω\mathrm{NC}\Omega.

The set {𝐪π:π​ is connected odd set partition}\{\mathbf{q}_{\pi}:\pi\text{ is connected odd set partition}\} must be algebraically independent because {𝐩π:π​ is connected odd set partition}\{\mathbf{p}_{\pi}:\pi\text{ is connected odd set partition}\} is algebraically independent and these two sets have the same cardinality in every degree. This proves (4). ∎

Remark 11.9.

The commutative version of Theorem 11.8 is a classical result that can be found in section 3.8 of [29].

11.3. Theta maps for noncommutative symmetric functions

We define the noncommutative symmetric functions NSym\mathrm{NSym} to be the Hopf subalgebra of NCSym\mathrm{NCSym} generated by HnH_{n} for all n≥1n\geq 1, where HαH_{\alpha} is the dual of MαM_{\alpha}. Thus we have

NSym=⟨Hn:n≥1⟩.\mathrm{NSym}=\langle H_{n}:n\geq 1\rangle.

Thus, the Hopf algebra NSym\mathrm{NSym} is the dual of QSym\mathrm{QSym}. In [4, Section 3], the authors defined the shuffle basis {Sα}\{S_{\alpha}\} for QSym\mathrm{QSym}. Let 𝐩α\mathbf{p}_{\alpha} be the dual of SαS_{\alpha}. The peak algebra for NSym\mathrm{NSym} is

Π∗=⟨𝐩n:n≥1,n is odd⟩,\Pi^{*}=\langle\mathbf{p}_{n}:n\geq 1,\text{$n$ is odd}\rangle,

and the theta map for NSym\mathrm{NSym}, ΘNSym=ΘQSym∗\Theta_{\mathrm{NSym}}=\Theta_{\mathrm{QSym}}^{*}, by [4, Theorem 3.8] is

ΘNSym:NSym→Π∗𝐩α↦{2​𝐩αif α is odd,0otherwise.\begin{array}[]{cccc}\Theta_{\mathrm{NSym}}:&\mathrm{NSym}&\rightarrow&\Pi^{*}\\ &\mathbf{p}_{\alpha}&\mapsto&\begin{cases}2\mathbf{p}_{\alpha}&\text{if $\alpha$ is odd},\\ 0&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}\end{array}

12. Combinatorial identities and conjectures

This section is a preparation for our main result on internal coproduct formula, and it has its own combinatorial interests.

Suppose ϕ=ϕ1|ϕ2​|⋯|​ϕℓ⁡(ϕ)\phi=\phi_{1}|\phi_{2}|\cdots|\phi_{\ell(\phi)} and ψ=ψ1|ψ2​|⋯|​ψℓ⁡(ψ)\psi=\psi_{1}|\psi_{2}|\cdots|\psi_{\ell(\psi)}. Remark 12.10.

From Corollary 12.8, to understand the coefficients Cφϕ​ψC_{\varphi}^{\phi\psi}, it suffices to understand the case where ϕ=1|2​|⋯|​n\phi=1|2|\cdots|n. In this case, ψ=1…α1|(α1+1)…α2|⋯|(αℓ⁡(ψ)−1+1)⋯n\psi=1\dots\alpha_{1}|(\alpha_{1}+1)\dots\alpha_{2}|\cdots|(\alpha_{\ell(\psi)-1}+1)\cdots n. Therefore, we can write the coefficients as CφαC^{\alpha}_{\varphi} where α⊧n\alpha\models n is a composition.

If every block of φ\varphi is contained in some block of ψ\psi, then ℓ⁡(ψ∧ζ)=ℓ⁡(ζ)\ell(\psi\land\zeta)=\ell(\zeta) for all ζ≥φ\zeta\geq\varphi. In this case, it can be deduced that Cφϕ​ψ=0C_{\varphi}^{\phi\psi}=0 unless φ∈𝒞ϕψ\varphi\in\mathscr{C}_{\phi}^{\psi}. If Problem 12.7 is true, then ψ=ϕ\psi=\phi implies Cφϕ​ψC_{\varphi}^{\phi\psi} is non-negative. A cancellation-free formula for Cφϕ​ψC_{\varphi}^{\phi\psi} remains open.

Conjecture 12.11.

By taking the special case of ψ=ϕ\psi=\phi in Lemma 12.5, we have that if the Conjecture 12.7 is true and if nn is even, then

∑k=1n/2(n2​k−1)​2n−2​k​(∑m=02​k−1(−1)m​E​(2​k−1,m))=2n−1.\sum_{k=1}^{n/2}\binom{n}{2k-1}2^{n-2k}\left(\sum_{m=0}^{2k-1}(-1)^{m}E(2k-1,m)\right)=2^{n-1}.

We would like to remark that Conjecture 12.7 has recently been confirmed by Zhao, Lin and Zang [47] using the method of generating functions. In addition, they prove a qq-analogue of Conjecture 12.11. They also provide two interesting and unexpected applications in enumerative combinatorics. The first one is that Conjecture 12.11 leads to a simple proof of that the Genocchi numbers are odd. This non-trivial fact was traditionally proved by several sophisticated methods, and no simple proof was known. As the second application, an alternative proof of Foata’s divisibility property of qq-tangent numbers is obtained as a consequence of the qq-analogue of Conjecture 12.11.

13. The peak algebra as a left co-ideal of NCQSym\mathrm{NCQSym} under the internal coproduct

The goal of this section is to prove that NC​Π\mathrm{NC}\Pi is a left co-ideal of NCQSym\mathrm{NCQSym} under the internal coproduct. In NCQSym, one can define (cf. [11]) an internal coproduct Δ∘:NCQSym→NCQSym⊗NCQSym\Delta^{\circ}:\mathrm{NCQSym}\to\mathrm{NCQSym}\otimes\mathrm{NCQSym} via the substitution f⁡(𝐱)↦f⁡(𝐱𝐲)↦f⁡(𝐱)⊗f⁡(𝐲)f(\mathbf{x})\mapsto f(\mathbf{xy})\mapsto f(\mathbf{x})\otimes f(\mathbf{y}) with {𝐱i​𝐲j}\{\mathbf{x}_{i}\mathbf{y}_{j}\} ordered lexicographically. Together with the regular product, mm, of power series, (NCQSym,m,Δ∘)(\mathrm{NCQSym},m,\Delta^{\circ}) forms an ungraded bialgebra.

The internal coproduct is given by

Δ∘​(𝐌ϕ)=∑ψ∧φ=ϕ𝐌ψ⊗𝐌φ.\Delta^{\circ}(\mathbf{M}_{\phi})=\sum_{\psi\land\varphi=\phi}\mathbf{M}_{\psi}\otimes\mathbf{M}_{\varphi}.

Note that φ∧ψ≠ψ∧φ\varphi\land\psi\neq\psi\land\varphi in general, so Δ∘\Delta^{\circ} is not cocommutative. Since ψ∧φ=ϕ\psi\land\varphi=\phi implies ψ≤ϕ\psi\leq\phi, we will use the following refined formula

Δ∘​(𝐌ϕ)=∑ψ≤ϕψ∧φ=ϕ𝐌ψ⊗𝐌φ.\Delta^{\circ}(\mathbf{M}_{\phi})=\sum_{\psi\leq\phi\atop\psi\land\varphi=\phi}\mathbf{M}_{\psi}\otimes\mathbf{M}_{\varphi}.

We are ready to prove the main theorem of this section.

14. Representation-theoretic interpretations of peak algebras and theta maps

In this section, we find representation-theoretic interpretations of the theta maps for the Hopf algebra of symmetric functions and noncommutative symmetric functions.

14.1. Symmetric functions

Let Irr⁡(G){\rm Irr}(G) be the set of irreducible characters of the finite group GG and cf⁡(G){\rm cf}(G) denote the space of the class functions of GG.

The space

cf⁡(𝔖∙)=⨁n≥0cf⁡(𝔖n){\rm cf}(\mathfrak{S}_{\bullet})=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}{\rm cf}(\mathfrak{S}_{n})

is a Hopf algebra with the product and coproduct

f.g=Ind(f.g)=Ind𝔖n×𝔖m𝔖n+m(f⊗g)f.g={\rm Ind}(f.g)={\rm Ind}_{\mathfrak{S}_{n}\times\mathfrak{S}_{m}}^{\mathfrak{S}_{n+m}}(f\otimes g)

and

Res⁡(f)=⨁i+j=nRes𝔖i⊗𝔖j𝔖n​(f),{\rm Res}(f)=\bigoplus_{i+j=n}{\rm Res}_{\mathfrak{S}_{i}\otimes\mathfrak{S}_{j}}^{{\mathfrak{S}}_{n}}(f),

respectively, where f∈𝔖nf\in{\mathfrak{S}}_{n} and g∈𝔖mg\in{\mathfrak{S}}_{m}. This Hopf algebra is isomorphic to the Hopf algebra of symmetric functions Sym\mathrm{Sym} using the Frebenius characteristic map

chSym:cf⁡(𝔖∙)→Sym{\rm ch}_{\mathrm{Sym}}:{\mathrm{cf}}({\mathfrak{S}}_{\bullet})\rightarrow\mathrm{Sym}

give by

zλ​δλ↦pλz_{\lambda}\delta_{\lambda}\mapsto p_{\lambda}

where zλ=1m1​m1!​2m2​m2!​3m3​m3!​…​nmn​mn!z_{\lambda}=1^{m_{1}}m_{1}!2^{m_{2}}m_{2}!3^{m_{3}}m_{3}!\dots n^{m_{n}}m_{n}! such that λ\lambda has mim_{i} parts equal to ii.

For f,g∈cf⁡(G)f,g\in{\mathrm{cf}}(G), define

f⊙gf\odot g

give by

(f⋅g)​(a)=f⁡(a)​g​(a)(f\cdot g)(a)=f(a)g(a)

for all a∈Ga\in G. Also, for any f∈cf⁡(G)f\in{\mathrm{cf}}(G), define

given by

(f⊙−)(g)=(f⊙g).(f\odot-)(g)=(f\odot g).

In the following theorem, we show that the following functor describes ΘSym\Theta_{\mathrm{Sym}},

Θcf⁡(𝔖∙)|cf⁡(𝔖n)=Ind∘((sgn⊙−)⊗(𝟙⊙−))∘Res\Theta_{{\mathrm{cf}}({\mathfrak{S}}_{\bullet})}|_{{\mathrm{cf}}({\mathfrak{S}}_{n})}={\rm Ind}\circ(({\mathrm{sgn}}\odot-)\otimes(\mathbbm{1}\odot-))\circ{\rm Res}

is a Hopf algebra by the representation theoretic functors Inf{\rm Inf} and Dn{\rm Dn} in [7, (3.1) and (3.2)] that we describe them combinatorially. In the following theorem, we show that for each α⊨n\alpha\vDash n, the representation-theoretic interpretation of ΘNSym\Theta_{\mathrm{NSym}} is defined by

Θcf⁡(𝔖∙)​((sgn)α𝟙)={2​(sgn)α𝟙if α is odd,0otherwise.\Theta_{{\mathrm{cf}}({\mathfrak{S}}^{\bullet})}(({\mathrm{sgn}})_{\alpha}^{{\mathbbm{1}}})=\begin{cases}2({\mathrm{sgn}})_{\alpha}^{{\mathbbm{1}}}&\text{if $\alpha$ is odd,}\\ 0&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}

This suggests that there may be a functor in representation theory that gives us the theta map of cf⁡(𝔖∙){\mathrm{cf}}({\mathfrak{S}}^{\bullet}) as the characters map to characters.

Remark.

A family of supercharacter theories for the group of unipotent upper-triangular matrices, with inflation and restriction functors, provides a representation-theoretic interpretation of NCSym\mathrm{NCSym} [1]. It would be interesting to find a functor in representation theory that is equivalent to the theta map of NCSym\mathrm{NCSym}.

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.
